# Part 1: Data verification & tidy data

## 1.1 Data import

Keep only Sample id plus what verification, grouping and Part 2's figures
actually use - `ST`/`Serotype` renamed and coerced to character here so
nothing downstream touches the raw `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type` /
`SeroTypeFinder/SeroType` names again.

A note: I only verified/asked questions for the spelling and re-encoding - for the fields that are included in the downstream figures (or kept in this data)
ST, Serotype, Production, Species

```{r load data}
isolates_raw <- read_excel(
  here::here(params$results_xlsx),
  sheet = params$isolate_sheet
) %>%
  select(
    Sample, Year, 
    Case = sak,
    ST = `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type`,
    Serotype = `SeroTypeFinder/SeroType`,
    Production = driftsformnavn,
    Species = artnavn
  ) %>%
  mutate(ST = as.character(ST))
```

```{r initial glimpse}
glimpse(isolates_raw)
```

## 1.2 Completeness checks

One row per isolate, and the fields every downstream figure depends on
(year, ST, serotype, production type) must be complete.

```{r qc checks}
qc <- list(
  n_rows = nrow(isolates_raw),
  n_distinct_sample = n_distinct(isolates_raw$Sample),
  n_missing_year = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Year)),
  n_missing_case = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Case)),
  n_missing_ST = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$ST)),
  n_missing_serotype = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Serotype)),
  n_missing_production = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Production)),
  n_missing_species = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Species))
  )

qc

stopifnot(
  "one row per isolate expected" = qc$n_rows == qc$n_distinct_sample,
  "Year must be complete" = qc$n_missing_year == 0,
  "ST must be complete" = qc$n_missing_ST == 0,
  "Serotype must be complete" = qc$n_missing_serotype == 0,
  "Production must be complete" = qc$n_missing_production == 0
)
```

## 1.3 Category spelling / homogeneity check


`check_spelling_homogeneity()` flags pairs of values in a column that are
identical after trimming/casefolding ("case_or_whitespace" - safe to
auto-fix) or within a small edit distance ("possible_typo" - needs a human
read).

Tolerance differs by column: `Production`/`Species` are free text, so a
1-2 character difference is almost always a typo (`max_dist = 2`); `ST`/
`Serotype` are nomenclature codes where a 1-character difference is usually a
genuinely different code (`O1:H4` vs. `O1:H7`), so only exact
case/whitespace collisions are flagged (`max_dist = 0`).

```{r spelling checks}
spelling_flags <- bind_rows(
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Production, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Production"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Species, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Species"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$ST, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "ST"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Serotype, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "Serotype")
) %>%
  relocate(column)

spelling_flags

write_csv(spelling_flags, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "spelling_flags.csv"))
```

Findings, fixed below: `Production` has a known mojibake artifact
("Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon" vs. corrupted "Foreldredyr,
kj�ttproduksjon", 2 rows); `Species` has one genuine case duplicate
("Rowan ranger" vs. "Rowan Ranger" - the other near-neighbours are real,
distinct breed names and are correctly not flagged); `ST`/`Serotype` have
nothing flagged.

```{r fix flagged values}
isolates_fixed <- isolates_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Production = if_else(
      Production == "Foreldredyr, kj�ttproduksjon",
      "Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon",
      Production)
    )
```

## 1.4 Cleaning: production type (broiler / parent flock)
And transforming Norwegian to English 
```{r clean driftsform}
isolates <- isolates_fixed %>%
  mutate(
    production_type = case_when(
      str_starts(Production, "Foreldredyr") ~ "Parent flock",
      Production == "Kjøttproduksjon" ~ "Broiler",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    production_type = factor(production_type, levels = c("Broiler", "Parent flock")),
    Year = as.integer(Year)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Species = case_when(
        Species == "Høns" ~ "Chicken",
        Species == "Hubbard" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Hubbard JA 787" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Ross" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross 308" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross rowan" ~ "Ross rowan",
        Species == "Rowan 308" ~ "Rowan 308",
        Species == "Rowan Ranger" ~ "Rowan ranger",
        Species == "Rustic gold" ~ "Rustic gold",
        Species == "Sasso" ~ "Sasso",
        TRUE ~ Species
      ),
      Species = factor(Species, levels = c(
        "Chicken",  "Ross 308", "Hubbard", "Ross rowan", "Rowan 308", "Rowan ranger", "Rustic gold", "Sasso")
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-Production)

stopifnot("production_type must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$production_type)) == 0)
stopifnot("Species must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$Species)) == 0)
count(isolates, production_type)
count(isolates, Species)

```

## 1.5 New variable: `variant` (ST-Serotype combination)

Requested format: `ST23-O78:H4`.

```{r variant column}
isolates <- isolates %>%
  mutate(
    ST = paste0("ST", ST),
    variant = paste0(ST, "-", Serotype)
    )

n_distinct(isolates$variant)  # 134 distinct ST-Serotype combinations observed
head(count(isolates, variant, sort = TRUE), 5)
```

## 1.6 ST, Serotype, variant contingency tables evaluation - top 5 / top 10 

### Variants 

```{r top n variant contingency}
#  data, group_col, top_n, other_cols, other_label = "Other" 
variant_contingency_top5 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 5, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype")) %>%
  mutate(top_n = 5L)

variant_contingency_top10 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 10, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype")) %>%
  mutate(top_n = 10L)



kept_vs_other <- function(contingency, top_n) {
  contingency %>%
    mutate(group_value = if_else(group_value == "Other", "other", "kept")) %>%
    summarise_contingency() %>%
    mutate(top_n = top_n, .before = 1)
}

variant_threshold_summary <- bind_rows(
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top5, 5),
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top10, 10)
)

variant_threshold_summary
```

The direct answer - for the top 5 (or top 10) variants, how many distinct ST
values and how many distinct Serotype values, and how many *other* ST/
Serotype values are left outside that set:

```{r top n variant counts wide}
variant_threshold_counts <- variant_threshold_summary %>%
  select(top_n, other_col, group_value, n_distinct_values) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = c(other_col, group_value),
    values_from = n_distinct_values,
    names_glue = "n_{other_col}_{group_value}"
  )

variant_threshold_counts
```

Reading this: keeping the top 5 variants names 5 STs and 5 serotypes, leaving
86 other STs and 114 other serotypes unnamed; the top 10 variants name 8 STs
and 10 serotypes, leaving 83 and 110. (Fewer than 10 *ST*s for the top-10
case because a couple of STs repeat across two different top-10 variants,
e.g. ST117 pairs with two different serotypes.)

Or per-value, not collapsed to kept/other - `summarise_contingency()` used directly on the
contingency table shows this for every individual kept variant too:

```{r top n variant contingency per value}
summarise_contingency(variant_contingency_top5)
```

## 1.7 Grouping for figures: top-5 + "Other" (three strategies)

The notes flag an open question for Figure 8: *"ST and serotype as top five,
or only ST as top five?"* - i.e. should ST and Serotype be bucketed to their
top 5 separately, or is there a third option of bucketing the combined
`variant` directly? All three are built here as reusable columns
(`top_n_other()`) so the comparison below has real numbers instead of
guesswork, and Figure 8's three examples can each pick whichever fits.

```{r grouped columns}
isolates <- isolates %>%
  mutate(
    ST_top5 = top_n_other(ST, 5, other_label = "Other"),
    # ST already reads "ST23" (prefixed in 1.5) - no second "ST" here
    ST_top5_label = if_else(ST_top5 == "Other", "Other ST", ST_top5),
    Serotype_top5 = top_n_other(Serotype, 5, other_label = "Other Serotype"),
    variant_top5 = top_n_other(variant, 5, other_label = "Other")
  )
```

```{r grouping comparison}
grouping_comparison <- tibble(
  strategy = c(
    "A: ST top5+Other, Serotype unrestricted",
    "B: ST top5+Other x Serotype top5+Other (crossed)",
    "C: variant (ST-Serotype) top5+Other, direct"
  ),
  n_categories_or_strata = c(
    isolates %>% distinct(ST_top5_label, Serotype) %>% nrow(),
    isolates %>% distinct(ST_top5_label, Serotype_top5) %>% nrow(),
    n_distinct(isolates$variant_top5)
  ),
  n_isolates_in_largest_other_bucket = c(
    sum(isolates$ST_top5 == "Other"),
    isolates %>% filter(ST_top5 == "Other", Serotype_top5 == "Other Serotype") %>% nrow(),
    sum(isolates$variant_top5 == "Other")
  )
) %>%
  mutate(pct_in_that_bucket = round(100 * n_isolates_in_largest_other_bucket / nrow(isolates), 1))

grouping_comparison
```

Reading this: **A** barely reduces visual complexity (122 of 134 combinations
survive, because Serotype - the wider axis at 115 levels - stays unrestricted)
and buries 43% of isolates in an ST-only "Other". **B** gets to a genuinely
readable 13 strata but its Other×Other cell alone hides 34% of isolates with
no ST or Serotype identity left. **C** is the most compact (6 categories) but
hides the most isolates (53%) - because it only credits a combination that
makes the *joint* top 5, not a common ST or common Serotype on their own.
There's no free lunch here; Figure 8's three examples below use A, C and A
again respectively (per the notes), so this table is the reference for judging
what each one is trading away.

## 1.8 Contingency tables + top 5 (ST, Serotype, variant)

```{r contingency tables}
st_contingency <- isolates %>%
  count(ST, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_isolates)) %>%
  mutate(is_top5 = ST %in% (isolates %>% count(ST, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_max(n, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(ST)))

serotype_contingency <- isolates %>%
  count(Serotype, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_isolates)) %>%
  mutate(is_top5 = Serotype %in% (isolates %>% count(Serotype, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_max(n, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(Serotype)))

variant_contingency <- isolates %>%
  count(variant, ST, Serotype, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_isolates)) %>%
  mutate(is_top5 = variant %in% (isolates %>% count(variant, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_max(n, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>% pull(variant)))

# full ST x Serotype contingency matrix (wide) - the "proper" contingency table
st_serotype_wide <- isolates %>%
  count(ST, Serotype, name = "n") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Serotype, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

top5_ST <- st_contingency %>% filter(is_top5)
top5_Serotype <- serotype_contingency %>% filter(is_top5)
top5_variant <- variant_contingency %>% filter(is_top5)
```

```{r export contingency tables}
contingency_tables <- list(
  ST = st_contingency,
  Serotype = serotype_contingency,
  Variant = variant_contingency,
  ST_x_Serotype_wide = st_serotype_wide,
  Top5_ST = top5_ST,
  Top5_Serotype = top5_Serotype,
  Top5_Variant = top5_variant,
  grouping_comparison = grouping_comparison
)

saveRDS(contingency_tables, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "contingency_tables.rds"))
write_xlsx(contingency_tables, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "contingency_tables.xlsx"))
```

```{r export tidy isolates}
isolates_tidy <- isolates %>%
```

# Part 2: Graph trials (draft, on verified data)

Collaborators like both sankey and pie chart plots: Figure 8's alluvial
diagrams are the Sankey-style flow charts (`ggalluvial`), Figure 7 is the
sized-bubble chart.

## Figure 7: variant composition (sized-bubble "pie" chart)

Not a literal radial pie - "size of the circles proportional to isolate
count" plus rotated *x-axis* labels means a proportional-bubble chart
(circle area, not radius, via `scale_size_area`). On-chart label is the
variant text only (`ST23-O78:H4`); counts and sent-case (insendelse) numbers
go to a supplementary table instead. Top 10 variants by isolate count (the
top5+Other bucketing from Part 1 would dilute the point of naming the common
ones); the rest is exactly what the supplementary table is for.

```{r figure7 data}
fig7_top_n <- 10

fig7_top_variants <- isolates %>%
  count(variant, name = "n_total") %>%
  slice_max(n_total, n = fig7_top_n, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(variant)

fig7_data <- isolates %>%
  filter(variant %in% fig7_top_variants) %>%
  count(variant, production_type, name = "n_isolates") %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = rev(fig7_top_variants)))
```

```{r figure7 supplementary}
fig7_supplementary <- isolates %>%
  mutate(shown_in_fig7 = variant %in% fig7_top_variants) %>%
  group_by(variant, ST, Serotype) %>%
  summarise(
    n_isolates = n(),
    n_sent_cases = n_distinct(Case),
    shown_in_fig7 = first(shown_in_fig7),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_isolates))

write_xlsx(fig7_supplementary, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "fig7_variant_supplementary.xlsx"))
```

```{r figure7}
fig7 <- fig7_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = variant, y = production_type, size = n_isolates, color = production_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = variant), size = 2.4, color = "grey15", vjust = -1.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 22, breaks = c(10, 25, 50, 100, 200)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2], guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Most common ST × Serotype variants",
    subtitle = paste0("Top ", fig7_top_n, " variants by isolate count; counts and sent cases in the supplementary table, not on the chart"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    size = "Isolates (n)\ncircle area ∝ count"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

fig7
save_apec_plot(fig7, "fig7_variant_bubble.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = 26, height = 12)
```

## Figure 8: three ST × Serotype flow examples (Sankey/alluvial)

Grouped to top-5 + "Other" rather than filtered by a count threshold, so
every isolate is represented somewhere (a named stratum or "Other"), none
dropped.

### Example 1: Year → ST (top 5 + Other) → Serotype (unrestricted)

Serotype is *not* bucketed here, so that axis still carries ~115 levels -
likely to look tangled; kept as the literal example requested rather than an
expected win.

```{r figure8 example1 data}
ex1_data <- isolates %>%
  count(Year, ST_top5_label, Serotype, production_type, name = "n")

ex1_year_order <- as.character(sort(unique(ex1_data$Year)))

ex1_st_order <- ex1_data %>%
  mutate(year_pos = match(as.character(Year), ex1_year_order)) %>%
  group_by(ST_top5_label) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(year_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(ST_top5_label)

ex1_serotype_order <- ex1_data %>%
  mutate(st_pos = match(ST_top5_label, ex1_st_order)) %>%
  group_by(Serotype) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(st_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(Serotype)

ex1_data <- ex1_data %>%
  mutate(
    Year_f = factor(as.character(Year), levels = ex1_year_order),
    ST_top5_label = factor(ST_top5_label, levels = ex1_st_order),
    Serotype = factor(Serotype, levels = ex1_serotype_order)
  )
```

```{r figure8 example1}
fig8_ex1 <- ex1_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = Year_f, axis2 = ST_top5_label, axis3 = Serotype, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/5, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Year", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "Example 1: Year × ST (top 5 + Other) × Serotype",
    subtitle = "ST bucketed to top 5 + \"Other ST\"; Serotype not bucketed (~115 levels) - compare against Examples 2/3",
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

fig8_ex1
save_apec_plot(fig8_ex1, "fig8_example1_year_st5_serotype.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = 32, height = 26)
```

### Example 2: Production type → Year → variant (top 5 + Other, kept)

Combined `variant` axis instead of separate ST/Serotype axes - grouping
strategy **C** from the comparison table (top 5 variants + "Other", 6
categories total, ~53% of isolates in "Other" but every isolate still counted
somewhere).

```{r figure8 example2 data}
ex2_data <- isolates %>%
  count(production_type, Year, variant_top5, name = "n")

ex2_year_order <- as.character(sort(unique(ex2_data$Year)))

ex2_variant_order <- ex2_data %>%
  mutate(year_pos = match(as.character(Year), ex2_year_order)) %>%
  group_by(variant_top5) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(year_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(variant_top5)

ex2_data <- ex2_data %>%
  mutate(
    Year_f = factor(as.character(Year), levels = ex2_year_order),
    variant_top5 = factor(variant_top5, levels = ex2_variant_order)
  )
```

```{r figure8 example2}
fig8_ex2 <- ex2_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(axis1 = production_type, axis2 = Year_f, axis3 = variant_top5, y = n)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = 1/5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/5, fill = "grey95", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 2.0) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Production type", "Year", "Variant"), expand = c(0.08, 0.08)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "Example 2: Production type × Year × Variant (top 5 + Other)",
    subtitle = "Variant (ST-Serotype) bucketed directly to its top 5 + \"Other\" - nothing excluded",
    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

fig8_ex2
save_apec_plot(fig8_ex2, "fig8_example2_production_year_variant5.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = 30, height = 22)
```

### Example 3: Production type → ST (top 5 + Other) → Serotype (unrestricted)

Same idea as Example 1, minus the year axis, production type first.

```{r figure8 example3 data}
ex3_data <- isolates %>%
  count(production_type, ST_top5_label, Serotype, name = "n")

ex3_st_order <- ex3_data %>%
  group_by(ST_top5_label) %>%
  summarise(n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(ST_top5_label)

ex3_serotype_order <- ex3_data %>%
  mutate(st_pos = match(ST_top5_label, ex3_st_order)) %>%
  group_by(Serotype) %>%
  summarise(bary = weighted.mean(st_pos, w = n), n_total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(bary, desc(n_total)) %>%
  pull(Serotype)

ex3_data <- ex3_data %>%
  mutate(
    ST_top5_label = factor(ST_top5_label, levels = ex3_st_order),
    Serotype = factor(Serotype, levels = ex3_serotype_order)
  )
```

```{r figure8 example3}

  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2]) +
  labs(
    title = "Example 3: Production type × ST (top 5 + Other) × Serotype",

    x = NULL, y = "Isolates", fill = "Production type"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```
